clue.text: Faculty is objective about lecturer

indicators.note: the word for objective is placed around the lecturer's letter

parts.note: fair means impartial, objective
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer, as on a learner's plate

explanation.surface: A university department claims to be impartial towards one of its lecturers.
explanation.definitionFit: A flair is a natural talent or aptitude, which is one sense of a faculty.

clue.text: Single-minded law enforcement agent keeps leaders of organised crime under surveillance

indicators.note: the agent's word holds the initial letters inside it

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent in US slang

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A determined FBI agent watches the mob bosses closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaders are taken from four words: organised, crime, under, surveillance.
explanation.definitionFit: Focused means concentrating on one aim, so single-minded.

clue.text: Realignment of earth in gas giant is contrary to nature

indicators.note: realigning the letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Rearranging planetary matter inside Jupiter would defy the natural order.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the grain means acting contrary to one's natural inclination, as against wood's fibres.

clue.text: Memorandum about account's opening balance

indicators.note: the memo word goes around the letter

parts.note: a reminder is a memorandum, a note to jog the memory

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A memo concerning the starting figure on a bank statement.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the balance outstanding.

clue.text: 39 winks, according to Spooner, is way to get woman into bed

definitions.text: way to get woman into bed

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so these two words trade their first sounds

parts.note: forty winks is a nap, so thirty-nine winks is a short one
a kip is a sleep, like winks in forty winks

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about seduction: a quick nap is the path to bed with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Forty winks is a nap, so '39 winks' is a SHORT KIP; swapping the opening sounds gives 'court ship'. KIP is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing someone is the traditional route to winning a partner, romantic and eventually intimate.

clue.text: Saint steps in to heal plague

indicators.note: the saint's letter enters the middle of the word for heal

parts.note: to cure is to heal

explanation.surface: A holy figure intervenes to cure an epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Plague as a verb means to afflict or torment, as does curse.

clue.text: Anxious, having not yet been paid

definitions.meaning: a bill still outstanding has not been settled

explanation.surface: A worker frets because the wages have not arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettled covers both being agitated and a debt still outstanding.

clue.text: Trunk with hollow rings within rings supporting treetop

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting letters sit below the top piece

parts.note: the top of the word tree is its first letter, T

indicators.note: the emptied letters sit inside the pair of rings

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring, so rings give two Os

indicators.note: hollow means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outside pair

explanation.surface: A tree trunk is pictured with hollow growth rings inside, holding up its crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties the first 'rings' to RS, which sits between two Os (the second 'rings'); T goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, excluding head and limbs.

clue.text: Did couple go some distance to be awkward?

parts.note: with go, did go becomes have left, so did gives the auxiliary have
a couple is two
to go is to leave, here in its past form left
feet is a measure of distance

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pair travelled a little way, in order to seem clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did couple go' splits round TWO: 'did go' is 'have left'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have two left feet is an idiom for being clumsy, especially when dancing.

clue.text: This punishment requires retraction of vacuous action to make change

indicators.note: the word for change needs the turned letters placed within it

parts.note: pence are small change, British coins

indicators.note: retraction means drawing back, so the letters read backwards
vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters remain

explanation.surface: A penalty that demands the withdrawal of a pointless act in order to bring about reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' leaves only the outside letters of action, and 'retraction of' turns them back to front; PENCE is British small change.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is a self-imposed punishment as atonement for wrongdoing.

clue.text: One captivating female singer carries gun

indicators.note: the singer's name holds the weapon inside it

parts.note: Cher is the American pop singer
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A beguiling woman singer turns out to be packing a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who charms or enchants others is literally captivating them.

clue.text: Fought against introduction of extras in short series

indicators.note: the two letters are put inside the shortened series
short means the last letter is cut off the word for series

parts.note: a string is a series, as in a string of victories
V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone resisted bringing in additional items to a brief run of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims STRING to STRIN, and V plus E goes in to make STRIVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Striven is the past participle of strive, to struggle or contend, as in having fought for something.

clue.text: Feeling transported about New Age

indicators.note: the word for transported goes around the other letters

parts.note: sent means carried away or delighted, as in 'that music sent me'
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone describes their emotional response to New Age spirituality as rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' reads as one familiar phrase, but its two words act separately and join in the other order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an emotion or attitude, a synonym of feeling.

clue.text: Temper's beginning to be ignored regularly

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for temper is dropped

parts.note: to temper is to soften or moderate

explanation.surface: Advice about anger: one's initial flare-up is often best overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Temper is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something often means doing it frequently, at repeated intervals.

clue.text: Conducted 4 across square

definitions.meaning: to have conducted a courtship is to have gone out with someone romantically
square means old-fashioned, out of touch

explanation.surface: Someone courted a person regarded as hopelessly unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated means both went out with romantically and looking old-fashioned.

clue.text: Aggressive corporations turning tail after company's intervention

indicators.note: the abbreviation for company steps in between the other letters
the tail of the word, its last two letters, swap round

parts.note: corporation is jocular slang for a large belly
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Big businesses become hostile, retreating after a firm meddles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporations' looks like big business, but it is jocular British slang for paunches; 'turning tail' swaps only the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose describes someone eager to fight, warlike in manner.

clue.text: One might precede 4 across land? I'd be there first surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters land in an unexpected new order
first takes the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone imagines arriving in a country ahead of everyone else, to their astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranged meeting between strangers can be the start of wooing and romance.

clue.text: Deceitful villains in ceremonial guards

indicators.note: the phrase guards the answer's letters within it

explanation.surface: Villains disguised in ceremonial guard uniforms are being dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere means not genuine, pretending feelings one lacks.

clue.text: Safe to lose time and ride around without rushing

indicators.note: the letter for time is taken away from the word for safe

parts.note: unhurt means safe, uninjured

indicators.note: around signals the letters of ride are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cyclist is told it is safe to take a leisurely ride without hurrying.
explanation.walkthrough: UNHURT loses T to give UNHUR, then the anagram of RIDE makes RIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurried means relaxed and leisurely, done at an easy pace.

clue.text: Implement silent reforms to support university

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting letters go beneath the university's letter
reforms means the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Quiet changes are brought in to prop up a university's finances.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, especially for the kitchen.

clue.text: Cook luncheon meat with leaves for old man

indicators.note: the word for leaves replaces the word for old man

parts.note: Spam is a brand of tinned luncheon meat
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
tea is made from leaves

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to prepare tinned meat with salad greens for an elderly gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is a method of cooking food in vapour from boiling water.

clue.text: Dome-shaped enclosure for animal reserve

indicators.note: shaped means the letters of the word are formed into a new arrangement

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A domed enclosure is described for a wildlife reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' looks like a nature reserve but means restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a noun means restraint or self-effacement, a synonym of modesty.

clue.text: Cube not displaying face in elevation

indicators.note: the face of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: height is elevation above the ground

explanation.surface: Describes a solid shape drawn in a side view with one face hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cube' looks geometric but it is the number: two cubed is eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a cube number, being two multiplied by itself three times.

clue.text: Hearing test

definitions.meaning: a court hearing of a case

explanation.definitionFit: A trial is both a court case being heard and a test of something.

clue.text: Controlled note reproduced round home

parts.note: do is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the word for reproduced goes round the word for home

parts.note: mated means bred, reproduced
in means at home

explanation.surface: A musical note copied out circles around a house, under someone's command.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominated means ruled over or held under power, which is to be controlled.

clue.text: Thick fog envelops easternmost part of England

indicators.note: the fog word wraps around the letter

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: on a map the east is the right-hand end, so the last letter

explanation.surface: A heavy fog shrouds the far eastern tip of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' looks like part of the fog but is the definition: the thick of something is its midst.
explanation.definitionFit: In the thick of things means in the midst, the centre of activity.

clue.text: Way dictator primarily augments ability to maintain power

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Idi Amin was the dictator of Uganda

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A tyrant's methods first boost his capacity to stay in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is endurance, the capacity to keep going and sustain effort.

clue.text: Nurse gets into revolutionary drug and becomes more intense

indicators.note: the nurse's letters go inside the turned-round drug
revolutionary means turning round, so the drug's word is read backwards

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse dabbling in a radical narcotic makes matters worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks political but signals turning the drug's name round, giving DEEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen is to intensify, as a crisis or colour can grow stronger.

clue.text: Librettist loses heart to complete stories, having minimal support from friends

indicators.note: the outer letters are joined to the pieces placed between them
losing its heart leaves only the first and last letters

parts.note: one means whole or complete, as in 'all in one'
lies are false stories

explanation.surface: A dispirited opera writer finishes his tales, feeling friendless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' sounds like despair but strips Librettist to its first and last letters, L and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Loneliest is the superlative of lonely, describing someone most isolated from companions.

clue.text: Record work extracted from disorder

indicators.note: the abbreviation for work is pulled out of the word for disorder

parts.note: entropy is a measure of disorder
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A record of a piece of music salvaged from chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry is an item written in a log, diary or register.
